text:
jess: Quick heads up — I hit a confusing behavior while validating v2 migration examples. Some of our v2 docs still show a top-level "model" field in request bodies, and the runtime shim will silently map to an alias which can cause unexpected model variants in prod. Repro below.

omar: ugh. paste the repro steps?

jess: repro:
1) POST to /v2/invoke with body `\{"model\": \"redwood-13b\", \"input\": \"Tell me a joke\"}`
2) client shim converts body to use model_id if present in headers, alias resolver rewrites to `redwood-13b-gpu` for perf, and if that pool is full it falls back to `redwood-7b-quant` silently

tara: that silent fallback is the problem — apps expecting 13b quality might degrade.

jess: exactly. Proposal: docs should include a dedicated migration note "Avoid top-level 'model' in v2 payloads" and a short checklist + example replacements. Also add a docs-lint rule that flags "model"\s*: in files under /docs/v2/ and fail CI.

sam: I can add the linter rule and a quickfix script that rewrites model->model_id in examples. Will add tests. Branch: docs/fix/model-param-lint

omar: do we want the runtime to error instead? breaking change might alarm users. Suggest: runtime emits warning header X-Redwood-Warn: model-collision and docs show how to opt into strict enforcement via header `X-RW-Strict: true`.

jess: yep, docs should show both patterns — graceful compatibility (warn) and strict opt-in (error). Include example curl and py snippet.

ci-bot: Note: new docs-lint config must be added to .github/workflows/docs-ci.yml to run during PR checks.

sam: adding snippet examples now. curl example (windows-friendly alternative below):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v2/invoke \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "X-RW-Strict: true" \
  --data-binary '{"model_id":"redwood-13b","input":"Summarize the following..."}'
```

sam: python SDK example:  
```python
from redwood import Client
c = Client(api_key=os.getenv("RW_TOKEN"))
resp = c.invoke(model_id="redwood-13b", input="Summarize...")
print(resp.output)
```

tara: include a migration checklist entry: run `scripts/find-legacy-models.sh` (I added it to repo) and run `make smoke-migration` which executes a small matrix of model_id responses to detect regressions. Add this to the guide.

jess: good. Also add a short table mapping common legacy docs -> replacement (e.g., `model` -> `model_id`, show header example). And add a line about alias maps: "Aliases like redwood-13b -> redwood-13b-gpu / redwood-13b-quant can change latency/quality".

omar: I'm editing the deprecation notice page to include a small blurb: "If your app relies on exact model variant, pin model_id and enable X-RW-Strict." Will push a PR.

sam: I'm opening PR 5902 (draft) with linter, quickfix script, updated examples, and tests. CI will run docs-lint.

publish-bot: Scheduled docs publish window: 2026-03-24T04:30Z if PRs are merged.

jess: can someone from SDKs confirm they'll add client-side warn mapping? pinging @sdk-js and @sdk-py in the thread.

omar: SDK leads replied in DMs: they'll add a minor update that maps legacy `model`->`model_id` and logs console.warn with link to migration guide. We'll coordinate releases with docs publish.

tara: tiny nit — prefer showing `--data-binary` in primary curl to avoid shell truncation; include `--data` variant for quick typing. Also include a note for Postman users.

sam: noted. I'll update PR. Anyone want to review 5902?

jess: reviewing now. once merged let's add redirects for any old example pages under /docs/examples/* that used top-level model. I can run a quick grep and open redirects PR.

sam: grep found 7 files, will include redirect map entries in PR as well.

jess: great. if no objections, let's mark this thread as follow-up in docs sync and close after PR merges. :white_check_mark:

omar: LGTM.
